explanation: Q1 checks if a customer has all distinct products by comparing COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) directly to the total distinct products in PRODUCT. Q2 first removes duplicate (customer, product) pairs, then counts the number of distinct products per customer. The difference arises when a customer has multiple entries for the same product, but Q1's COUNT(DISTINCT) and Q2's COUNT(1) may behave differently due to grouping logic.
counterexample_dsp: Create a scenario where PRODUCT has 2 products (P1, P2). Customer A has (P1, P2) and Customer B has (P1, P1, P2). Q1 will return both customers since COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) is 2 for both. Q2 will also return both, but if PRODUCT had 3 products and Customer B has only 2 distinct products, Q2 would exclude them.
